commits.message:
A Viewport render that holds its content commits nothing: offset, followed range and queued moves wait for a render that draws (rich-widgets-hmk1.0ix)

Review of #473: a held render kept the last length but took its rows from
the empty render, so under a ceiling or no height the follow re-ensure moved
the offset, canScrollBy reported moves past the last full view, queued moves
resolved while nothing was shown, and the gutter drew zero rows.

A Viewport whose content is handed no column keeps its offset, and a ListView keeps its wheel position (rich-widgets-hmk1.0ix)

Law pass over presence and render-time state. A Viewport drawn no wider
than its gutter held its content and clamped its offset against the
nothing that came back, resetting it to 0; it now keeps the length the
last drawing render found. A ListView whose items were held followed the
empty range they named, which read as a selection move and undid the
wheel. Also reattaches withBoundedWidth's doc comment, which measuring
had been inserted below.

A widget its container hands no column is held in the view, not drawn, so it keeps focus and nothing renders for it (rich-widgets-hmk1.kvc) (#472)

* A widget its container hands no column is held in the view, not drawn, so it keeps focus and nothing renders for it (rich-widgets-hmk1.kvc)

protocol's render is the one reporter of what the view holds: RenderOptions.onDraw,
called by WidgetBase, becomes onPresent(renderable, "drawn" | "held"), called by
render for every renderable it is asked for. Under one column a renderable is held:
render walks the Composite.contents() of what it holds, reports each held, and
renders nothing, so a Viewport's offset or a TextInput's scroll window is never
committed at a width that is not shown.

Every exported container implements Composite. The method is contents(), not the
children() the seam named, because Tree.children and Layout.children are already
Rich's names for subtrees and panes. test/renderables/contents.test.ts holds each
exported renderable's contents() to what its render draws.

WidgetApp settles focus over the widgets the frame holds, drawn or held, and exposes
them as WidgetApp.present.

* Tab from a widget held on no column moves to its neighbour in document order; review fixes (rich-widgets-hmk1.kvc)

The focus manager reads the view's document order and its on-screen widgets
from one FocusView, so settle takes no argument and next/prev step from the
current widget's place in the view rather than its place on screen.

Also: Panel's and Table's moved JSDocs back onto their members, one cellAt for
Table's blank-cell fallback, Composite says it commits no state rather than
that it is pure, and contents.test holds Table without its header and Tree with
its root hidden.

* A held widget paints no overlay, pinned with the terminal wide enough to show one (rich-widgets-hmk1.kvc)
